title: GoHighLevel Systems Architect: Coaching Scorecards, Custom Objects & Automation

facts: Post: build a weekly business performance and accountability system inside our existing GoHighLevel account.
Post: preserve every weekly submission as a separate historical record; use custom objects and associations where appropriate.
Post: weekly submission reminders, follow-up for missing submissions, confirmation and internal notifications, reliable handling of repeat submissions and duplicate triggers.
Post: coach-facing view, track historical performance and targets, identify missing data and clients who need attention, connect performance gaps to training resources and action plans.
Post asks for a redacted demo, screenshots or a walkthrough of a comparable project.
Personalization: business name stated in post. Greg appears in only one freelancer review, so no first name is used (U-006).

close.title: Measure the scorecards
close.accent: and what coaches do with them.
close.caption: Start from your current numbers, then track on-time scorecards, coach prep time, and gaps that get an action plan.

metrics.name: On-time scorecards
metrics.aim: More scorecards in by the deadline
metrics.definition: Weekly scorecards submitted by the Friday deadline, divided by all active coaching clients expected to submit that week, reported per week and per coach.

metrics.name: Coach prep time per client
metrics.aim: Less time gathering numbers before calls
metrics.definition: Minutes a coach spends collecting and checking a client's numbers before a coaching call, measured with a short weekly time log during an agreed observation period.

metrics.name: Flagged gaps with an action plan
metrics.aim: More gaps turned into a next step
metrics.definition: Scorecard metrics flagged below target that have a training resource and action plan assigned before the next coaching call, divided by all flagged metrics in the same period.

scenes.caption: The reminder goes out Monday. On Wednesday the workflow checks for this week's scorecard before anyone gets a second message.
scenes.beat: Every Monday the scorecard week opens and {{client.first}} gets a text with the {{week.id}} link. On Wednesday the workflow checks whether her {{week.id}} scorecard is on file. It isn't, so she gets one follow-up text and her coach, {{coach.first}}, gets an alert. If she had already submitted, she'd get a thank-you and nothing else.
